follow-up time: From postnatal day 7 to 36 weeks postmenstrual age (PMA) or discharge if sooner.
study type: Retrospective analysis of prospectively collected data
exposure: Epoch 2: Improved lactation staffing, introduction of high-protein formula, single-family room setting
cohort: 584 surviving infants with birth weight ≤1000 g and gestational age 24-29 weeks admitted to a single-center neonatal intensive care unit between July 3, 2005, and June 6, 2016.
finding: Implementation of a nutrition care bundle was associated with improved weight gain in extremely low birth weight infants.
